entity_title: Residencia legal permanente abierta a cualquier extranjero
fact_text: Uruguay grants permanent legal residence to any foreigner who intends to settle permanently, with no nationality quota or points test. A third-country (EU/US) professional can therefore apply directly for permanent residence, not only a temporary permit; the file is processed by the Direccion Nacional de Migracion.
evidence_quote: toda persona extranjera con ánimo de residir en forma permanente en el país

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Unlike most OECD destinations, Uruguay lets a non-national apply for PERMANENT residence up front rather than only a temporary permit; there is no nationality restriction or quota.

entity_title: Residencia temporaria por motivos laborales es acotada en el tiempo
fact_text: The work-based temporary legal residence is granted for a minimum of 6 months and a maximum of 2 years, and is renewable (prorrogable). It is open to any nationality relocating for employment or study.
evidence_quote: por un plazo mínimo de 6 meses y máximo de 2 años prorrogable

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR trap: the work permit is a time-boxed temporary residence (max 2 years, renewable) and a different track from the open permanent residence; it must be renewed before expiry or status lapses.

entity_title: Documentos extranjeros: apostilla o legalización y traductor público uruguayo
fact_text: Every foreign document added to a residence file must be apostilled or legalized (under Ley N° 15.441) and translated into Spanish by a Uruguayan sworn public translator; only documents issued by Brazil are exempt from translation. This covers civil-status, criminal-record and employment documents.
evidence_quote: Todo documento extranjero que se presente para ser agregado al expediente debe estar necesariamente apostillado o legalizado (de acuerdo a lo dispuesto en la Ley N° 15.441) y traducido al español por traductor público uruguayo, con la excepción de los emitidos por Brasil.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR-generalist trap: the translation must be by a URUGUAYAN sworn public translator; translations done in the origin country are not accepted, adding lead time and cost to every foreign document.

entity_title: La vía Mercosur no aplica a nacionales de terceros países
fact_text: Uruguay has a simplified residence track reserved for nationals of Mercosur member and associated states (Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Suriname, Guyana). A third-country national (EU/US) is NOT eligible for it and must use the ordinary residence procedure.
evidence_quote: Dirigida a personas extranjeras de nacionalidad de los países parte y asociados del Mercosur. (Argentina, Brasil, Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay, Perú, Ecuador, Colombia, Venezuela, Surinam y Guyana).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR trap: online advice about Uruguay's fast Mercosur residence does not apply to EU/US employees; they follow the general route with the full apostille and sworn-translation burden.

entity_title: Cédula de identidad con la residencia aún en trámite
fact_text: Foreigners born abroad whose residence is still in process (residencia en trámite), or who hold definitive or Mercosur residence, obtain and renew the Uruguayan cédula de identidad at the DNIC. When the back of the card shows a D.N.M. expediente number, renewal requires a Certificado Migratorio evidencing the residence file is progressing.
evidence_quote: Este trámite deberán hacerlo las personas nacidas en el exterior que tengan certificado de residencia en trámite, legal definitiva, o definitiva Mercosur

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious: a first cédula is issued while residence is only in trámite, but it is short-dated and will not renew without a fresh migration certificate; a stalled residence file silently blocks cédula renewal and therefore banking, health and payroll enrolment.

entity_title: Residencia fiscal por permanencia mayor a 183 días
fact_text: An individual becomes a Uruguayan tax resident by being present in the country more than 183 days during the calendar year; a sporadic absence of up to 30 consecutive days still counts as days of presence. This is independent of immigration status.
evidence_quote: quienes permanezcan más de 183 días durante el año civil en territorio nacional

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR trap: tax residency is triggered by physical presence, not by the residence permit; an assignee who crosses 183 days becomes Uruguayan tax-resident even on a temporary permit, and short trips home under 30 days do not reset the count.

fact_text: Tax residency can also be triggered by holding real-estate investment above 15:000.000 UI, or above 3.500.000 UI combined with at least 60 days of physical presence in the calendar year (for acquisitions made on or after 1 July 2020) — with no need to reach 183 days.
evidence_quote: una inversión en bienes inmuebles por un valor superior a 15:000.000 UI

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious: buying a home in Montevideo above the UI threshold can itself make an employee a Uruguayan tax resident regardless of days spent; UI thresholds are re-valued yearly, so confirm the current figure with counsel.

entity_title: Residencia fiscal por inversión empresarial que crea empleo
fact_text: Tax residency can be triggered by a direct or indirect investment in a company above 15.000.000 UI, made on or after 1 July 2020, that generates at least 15 new full-time direct dependent jobs during the calendar year.
evidence_quote: deben generar al menos 15 (quince) nuevos puestos de trabajo directo en relación de dependencia a tiempo completo durante el año civil

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious: an executive who sets up or funds a local entity that hires 15+ staff can acquire tax residency through the business-investment causal, not only through days present.

entity_title: Residencia fiscal por base de intereses económicos
fact_text: A person is also deemed a Uruguayan tax resident when Uruguay is the base of their economic interests — that is, when they generate a larger volume of gross income in Uruguay than in any other single country.
evidence_quote: genera en el país rentas de mayor volumen que en cualquier otro país (entendiéndose por tal mayor caudal de ingresos brutos)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious: even below 183 days, an assignee whose largest single-country income source becomes the Uruguayan payroll can be pulled into tax residency via the economic-interest test.

entity_title: Tax holiday para nuevos residentes fiscales
fact_text: New tax residents may elect, for foreign movable-capital income (e.g. interest and dividends), either to pay non-resident tax (IRNR) for the fiscal year of the residency change and the following ten fiscal years (the 10-years-plus-1 option), or to pay IRPF at a reduced 7% rate with no time limit.
evidence_quote: a) el IRNR, por el ejercicio fiscal en que se verifique el cambio de residencia a territorio nacional y durante los diez ejercicios fiscales siguientes (opción 10 años + 1), o b) el IRPF a la tasa 7% sin límite temporal.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: A genuine relocation draw and a common HR blind spot: for roughly a decade Uruguay lets new residents keep foreign passive income out of ordinary IRPF; the election and its timing are a pre-move tax-planning item to confirm with counsel.

entity_title: Alta obligatoria del trabajador dependiente en BPS
fact_text: When a company hires dependent workers it is legally obliged to register them with BPS (social security), report any changes, and file the monthly payroll (nomina) declaration of the employment relationship. A foreign employee on a local contract is enrolled in the Uruguayan social-security system from the start of employment.
evidence_quote: Cuando se contrata trabajadores dependientes, la empresa tiene la obligación de registrarlos ante BPS, informar las modificaciones que se produzcan y declarar en forma mensual los datos vinculados con la relación laboral.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: HR trap: enrolment is the EMPLOYER's legal duty and is automatic with the local contract, with no opt-out for a seconded foreign professional; BPS contributions fund both the pension (jubilacion) and FONASA health.

entity_title: Cobertura de salud FONASA para el trabajador y su familia
fact_text: Uruguay's Sistema Nacional Integrado de Salud regulates the right to health protection for all inhabitants through a National Health Insurance (SNS) funded by FONASA. An employed worker is covered, and the coverage is obligatorily extended to the worker's family group (spouse and dependent minor children).
evidence_quote: El Sistema Nacional Integrado de Salud reglamenta el derecho a la protección de salud de todos los habitantes del país, a través de un Seguro Nacional de Salud (SNS), financiado por el Fondo Nacional de Salud (Fonasa)

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Non-obvious for HR: the same page states coverage is extended obligatorily to the worker's nucleo familiar, so once on FONASA the employee's spouse and minor children get public health coverage through the worker's contribution, which can offset private family-insurance cost in the package.
